extracted.intended_audience: policy researchers, DoD/Navy managers and analysts implementing or evaluating OMB Circular A-76/Commercial Activities (CA) cost-comparison studies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for the Department of the Navy's implementation of the OMB Circular A-76 Commercial Activities program, including the phases of the cost-comparison process, PWS/PRS requirements, MEO development, costing rules, exemptions, and post-award monitoring concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four phases of CA program implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: The process ... consists of basically four phases: inventory, management review, cost comparison, and implementation of the results of the cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These four discrete phases form the structural framework for deciding who should perform governmental operations under the CA program; each phase has specific objectives and required actions described elsewhere (inventory identifies functions; management review assesses special circumstances; cost comparison performs the economic test; implementation carries out the decision).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventory phase: identification of commercial activities
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventory phase involves the identification of Navy activities ashore that can be performed by commercial sources. This includes all those functions that are not excluded because they are 'governmental in nature'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventory must classify functions and exclude those 'governmental in nature' per policy; accurate inventorying is prerequisite to any subsequent review or study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management review: identify special circumstances and exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The management review phase ... involves systematic examination and analysis by the activity to identify any special circumstances that would preclude performance of the function by a commercial source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During review, OPNAV (OP-443) examines each function to determine whether it should be retained in-house for national defense reasons and applies validated exemption criteria (see 'Valid reasons for national defense exemptions').

rubrics_metrics.name: Valid national defense exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Valid reasons for national defense exemptions ... include mobilization and contingency requirements, military training requirements, maintaining the Navy's sea/shore rotation base and depot and intermediate level maintenance requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These explicit exemption categories (documented in OPNAVINST 4860.6C) should be used to retain functions in-house where performance by commercial sources would conflict with these national defense needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case-by-case exemptions (core logistics/patient care)
rubrics_metrics.description: Other exemptions allowed on a case-by-case basis include those for core logistics functions and patient care at DOD hospitals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are discretionary exemptions that must be justified on a per-function basis during management review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiation procedures for CA review studies
rubrics_metrics.description: The process is initiated when the local command submits a review format via the chain of command to OPNAV (OP-443) with certain data specified by OPNAVINST 4860.6C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adherence to submission formats and required data is mandatory to get a function considered for a cost study; failure to supply required data can halt or delay a decision to conduct a cost comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the cost comparison phase
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of the cost comparison phase is to determine if it is more economical to perform the function in-house using government employees or to contract with a commercial firm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The analysis must compare estimated in-house costs (MEO) to contractor bids using the Cost Comparison Handbook methodology; the outcome drives implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Work Statement (PWS) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The task analysis involved in the development of the PWS must identify and quantify the output generated by the function. The PWS forms the basis of both the government's and commercial sources' cost estimations/bids and therefore must accurately reflect what is desired in terms of quality and performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PWS should specify work in terms of outcome rather than procedures ('specify work only in terms of its outcome, rather than in terms of the procedures used to achieve that outcome'); procedural matters are left to competing activities to allow flexibility and efficiency. Accurate task analysis is noted as one of the most difficult and critical tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of standard/generic PWSs
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizing the importance of the PWS ... standard or generic PWSs for the various functional areas have been developed. Completed DOD generic PWSs ... are being collected by the Defense Logistics Studies Information Exchange (DLSIE) ... for dissemination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field activities are encouraged to use or adapt developed generic PWSs to ensure consistency and completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Requirements Summary (PRS) and Acceptable Quality Level (AQL)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PWS also includes a section known as the Performance Requirements Summary (PRS) which stipulates the performance standards or quality levels that must be met. Included in the PRS, in addition to the Acceptable Quality Level (AQL), is a deduction percentage which approximates the level of importance that the activity assigns to each of the performance measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRS entries represent the most critical functions/outcomes; deduction percentages are used to compute monetary assessments against contractor billings for non-compliance. PRS items are intended to be objectively measurable and form the basis of contractor quality control and government quality assurance programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective measurability of performance standards
rubrics_metrics.description: These performance quality standards 'are designed to be objectively measurable, and quality control is part of the contractor's responsibility.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance metrics in the PRS must be quantifiable so QAEs can assess compliance and deductions can be applied consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Assurance program and QAEs
rubrics_metrics.description: Should the function be contracted out, the PRS will form the basis of both the contractor's Quality Control program and the government's Quality Assurance program. The Quality Assurance program ... consists of conducting regular surveillance to ensure contract (PWS) compliance using government employees known as Quality Assurance Evaluators (QAEs) or Contract Compliance Representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: QA programs should implement regular surveillance; while a formal QA program is not required for government performance, the MEO must still provide the capability to evaluate and clearly document performance to PWS standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management study objective and Most Efficient Organization (MEO)
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of the management study/review is to ensure that the in-house work force is organized and staffed as efficiently and effectively as possible ... Once this review has been conducted, the organization is restructured into what is termed as the Most Efficient Organization or MEO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MEO represents the in-house organization optimized for efficiency and is the basis for the in-house cost estimate used in bid comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of military positions to civilian for cost comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: If a function has been identified as a commercial activity ... any military positions in the function under study 'shall be converted to civilian positions for cost comparison purposes.' The cost estimate developed in conjunction with the MEO is for an 'all civilian' in-house operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost comparisons use an all-civilian MEO baseline; this conversion rule is mandatory for functions deemed commercial activities (except when exempted, e.g., sea/shore rotation).

rubrics_metrics.name: MEO costing rules per Cost Comparison Handbook
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed guidance for preparation of this estimate is contained in the Cost Comparison Handbook. Category and line-by-line computational techniques are included ... and include guidance on such factors as inflation, personnel costs, materials and supplies, depreciation, overhead, contract administration, conversion costs, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the handbook's standard cost factors and line-item computations to produce a uniform, defensible in-house cost estimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison rule: government's sealed bid vs lowest competent responsive private bidder
rubrics_metrics.description: The government's bid for providing the product or service is compared to that of the lowest, competent and responsive private bidder and a decision is made to either retain the function in-house ... or to contract out the function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision criterion is cost comparison against the lowest competent responsive bid (not necessarily lowest price only); ensure bidder competence and responsiveness are evaluated before comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost comparison methodology: incremental approach and standard cost factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost comparison methodology was changed from the complex full cost method to a simpler incremental approach. ... Many of the complex cost computations that were often contested were either eliminated or replaced by standard cost factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the simplified incremental approach and standard cost factors to shorten forms and reduce contested computations; refer to Cost Comparison Handbook for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor bid composition and MEO labor differential
rubrics_metrics.description: The contractor bids included an estimate of the contract administration costs (normally ranging from 4-8% of the MEO bid), but excluded the 10% of MEO personnel costs that are added before making the actual contract out decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing bids, remember to add the statutory/required 10% MEO labor differential to the contractor comparison or to the MEO as prescribed; consider contract administration estimates typically included in contractor bids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service Contract Act wage determination effect
rubrics_metrics.description: The Service Contract Act of 1965 provides for the establishment of minimum wages, benefits and working conditions ... The wage determination serves as a bottom limit for the contractor on employee wages and in certain cases reduces some of the contractor's cost flexibility in contract competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Department of Labor wage determinations where applicable; lack of a wage determination can distort initial contract pricing and later adjustments when determinations are established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award transaction costs to be considered (often ignored)
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-award transaction costs in excess of those anticipated by the pre-award cost comparison process are often ignored. These areas include litigation costs, conversion costs, contract administration costs in excess of that allowed for in the cost comparison process, quality or substandard performance costs, or the cost of contingency operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysts should account for likely post-award costs when assessing net benefits; absence of a formal accounting system for these costs can bias decisions toward contracting out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for formal post-award monitoring/accounting system
rubrics_metrics.description: The post-award results of the CA process are rather loosely monitored and there is no formal accounting system that captures litigation costs, conversion costs, contract administration costs ... quality or substandard performance costs, or the cost of contingency operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish monitoring and accounting mechanisms to capture hidden or post-award transaction costs to inform future cost comparisons and policy debate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance gaps: contractor default, bankruptcy, and resource cuts
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no formal guidance to commands on how to accomplish the 'contracted out' function in the event of contractor default or bankruptcy or how to manage resource/fund cuts in the event of reduced budgets for those functions that are now performed commercially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy should include contingency plans and guidance for transition back to government performance, resolution of defaults, and handling budget reductions for contracted functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance evaluation methods and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance assessments were made primarily by using observation (in all cases) and the results of Quality Assurance inspections (in all but one of the cases). Additionally, 56% indicated that performance was evaluated using external inspection results and 78% said customer satisfaction measures were used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a combination of observation, QA inspections, external inspections, and customer satisfaction measures; however, objective pre/post-award performance statistics were rarely provided—indicating the need for better data systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of deductions and Contract Discrepancy Reports for substandard performance
rubrics_metrics.description: A majority (56%) of the commands queried had taken deductions for substandard performance despite acceptable performance overall. Four commands also indicated that they had issued Contract Discrepancy Reports both in addition to and in support of deductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracts should include deduction clauses and procedures for documenting and enforcing deductions (e.g., via Contract Discrepancy Reports); track deduction amounts as a performance indicator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract award procedures and evidence requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Two respondents indicated that a sealed bid was used to award the contract, ... the majority of the activities used negotiated procurement to make the award. Technical proposals were used in a majority of the awards (56%). Only 44% of the activities were directly involved in the pre-award survey before contract award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice of procurement method (sealed bid, negotiated, small business set-aside) and use of technical proposals affect evaluation and oversight. Conduct pre-award surveys to assess financial integrity and technical competence; ensure technical proposals and pre-award surveys are used where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling and selection criteria for CA studies (research)
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies were selected by functional code (S713 for Food Service, T801 for Storage and Warehousing) as either Primary or Secondary Function Studied. Multi-function or umbrella contracts are coded using one primary function code with others listed as secondary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When sampling CA studies for analysis, use function codes to identify relevant cases and account for multi-function coding practices; accessibility and geographic constraints may shape practical sample choices.
